title: Gland vs Akums vs Kwality: Comparing India's Pharma CDMO Growth Pipelines
excerpt: India's contract drug manufacturing sector is booming as global pharma outsources more production, but the three leading listed CDMOs are betting on very different strategies to capture that growth.
body:
• Gland Pharma is making its biggest bet on GLP-1 injectables, expanding cartridge fill-finish capacity from 40 million to 140 million units — positioning itself as one of the few Indian CDMOs with integrated GLP-1 manufacturing.
  • Akums Drugs commands roughly 30% of India's outsourced domestic pharma manufacturing and is pushing into European regulated markets, with a Zambian government joint venture and its first commercial export batch shipped to Switzerland.
  • Kwality Pharmaceuticals, the smallest of the three, posted the fastest growth — 36% revenue and 69% profit increases in FY26 — and recently received CDSCO approval to begin preclinical batches of pembrolizumab, its entry into biosimilars.
  • The global CDMO market is projected to reach $375 billion by 2031, with India's share growing faster than the global average thanks to cost advantages and regulatory approvals.

Three Strategies, One Tailwind

India's pharmaceutical contract development and manufacturing sector has become one of the fastest-growing segments in the country's pharma industry. The global CDMO market, valued at roughly $259 billion in 2025, is projected to reach $375 billion by 2031 at a 6.3% compound annual growth rate, according to ResearchAndMarkets. India's share is growing even faster, driven by cost advantages, the largest number of U.S. FDA-approved plants outside America, and increasing willingness among global pharma companies to outsource everything from API synthesis to fill-finish operations.

Among India's listed CDMOs, Gland Pharma, Akums Drugs, and Kwality Pharmaceuticals represent three distinct approaches to capturing this opportunity. Their strategies differ by scale, market focus, and therapeutic bet.

Gland Pharma: The GLP-1 Play

Gland Pharma, majority-owned by China's Fosun Pharma, is the most established of the three in regulated markets. The Hyderabad-based company generated $340 million from the U.S. alone in FY26, launching 31 products during the year. Its growth strategy rests on four pillars: geographic expansion, portfolio diversification, strategic collaborations, and operational excellence.

The company's headline bet is on GLP-1 receptor agonists — the blockbuster class of diabetes and weight-loss drugs including semaglutide and liraglutide. Gland has expanded its cartridge fill-finish capacity from 40 million to 140 million units per year, making it one of the few CDMOs in India with integrated GLP-1 manufacturing capabilities. It has signed eight contracts with generic manufacturers and expects six to seven more as patents expire across markets from India and Canada (FY26) to the U.S. (FY30).

The company is also scaling three dedicated CDMO production lines expected to be commercialized from FY28, with one projected to add 5-6% to its current U.S. sales. Its acquisition of France-based Cenexi is pivoting from low-margin, high-volume products to higher-value formats like pre-filled syringes and lyophilized vials.

Akums Drugs: The Domestic Giant Going Global

Akums Drugs & Pharmaceuticals is India's largest CDMO by domestic market share, commanding roughly 30% of outsourced manufacturing for Indian pharma companies. The New Delhi-based company has developed over 4,100 commercialized formulations across more than 60 dosage forms, serving 26 of the top 30 Indian pharma firms.

Revenue reached ₹4,178 crore in FY24, growing at a 15.8% CAGR over five years. At a current P/E of about 24, it trades at a significant discount to peers in the 50-60 range — though profitability has been uneven, with net profit margins compressed by falling API prices.

Akums is now pushing into regulated export markets. The company completed a European GMP audit for its Plant 2 and shipped its first commercial batch of Dapagliflozin tablets to Switzerland. A supply of Rivaroxaban tablets to Europe is projected for the current quarter, with more than ten active European dossiers in the pipeline. The company has also entered a joint venture with the Zambian government to establish a manufacturing plant in Lusaka, with production anticipated by 2028.

Kwality Pharmaceuticals: Small but Fast

Kwality Pharmaceuticals is the smallest of the three by a wide margin — its market capitalization of roughly ₹1,618 crore places it firmly in micro-cap territory. But its growth rate is the fastest. FY26 revenue rose 36% year-on-year to ₹506 crore, while net profit surged 69% to ₹67 crore. Its return on equity of 16.4% and return on capital employed of 18.4% are strong for its size.

The Amritsar-based company recently received CDSCO approval to initiate preclinical pilot batches of pembrolizumab, the biosimilar of Merck's blockbuster immunotherapy Keytruda. This marks Kwality's entry into the high-value biologics space, building on its earlier commercialization of PEGylated-Asparaginase, its first biologic product.

The stock has been a standout performer, delivering a five-year return of roughly 1,949%. But institutional investors remain largely absent — foreign institutions hold just 0.5%, mutual funds hold zero, and the shareholder base is dominated by retail investors. The stock's 52% annualized volatility reflects this thin institutional ownership.

The Outlook

Each company faces distinct risks. Gland Pharma's heavy bet on GLP-1 fill-finish capacity could face margin pressure if too many competitors build similar lines. Akums must execute on its European expansion while managing API price headwinds. Kwality needs institutional validation and must prove its biologics ambitions are more than aspirational.

The structural tailwind, however, is real. As Schedule M compliance requirements tighten in India, smaller manufacturers are increasingly outsourcing to established CDMOs. Globally, patent expiries on GLP-1 drugs, rising biologics complexity, and fill-finish bottlenecks are creating demand that India's cost-competitive manufacturers are well-positioned to capture.
nri_angle: India's CDMO sector expansion is driven in part by global pharmaceutical companies seeking cost-effective manufacturing partners, creating investment opportunities in a sector with strong structural growth.
